I was unable to land the required fix. The target behavior — `ModelAdmin.lookup_allowed()` incorrectly raising `DisallowedModelAdminLookup` when a foreign key is used as a primary key (e.g. `restaurant__place__country`) — is NOT addressed.

What happened: my edits to `django/contrib/admin/options.py` repeatedly failed to apply. The `str_replace` operations either reported "old_str equals new_str" (no change) or corrupted adjacent lines, which I then reverted. The only edit that actually landed was an accidental insertion of a blank line at line 478-479 (a whitespace-only change), which does not alter behavior. The core logic at lines 467-470 remains unchanged.

The public regression selection (`modeladmin`, 162 tests) reports `passed: true`, but that reflects the unmodified baseline behavior, not a fix. The host feature test `test_lookup_allowed_foreign_primary` will still fail with `AssertionError: False is not True`.

Intended fix (not applied): in `BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed`, the relation-part skipping logic at lines 467-470 treats any field present in `prev_field.path_infos[-1].target_fields` as a concrete-inheritance parent link. For a FK-as-primary-key (a `OneToOneField(..., primary_key=True)` that is not a parent link), this wrongly drops the field from `relation_parts`, producing `restaurant__country` instead of `restaurant__place__country`. The correct behavior is to only skip the field when it is an actual concrete-inheritance parent link (i.e. `field.remote_field.parent_link` is true), so the full lookup is preserved and matched against `list_filter`.

This is an honest report of an incomplete task: no functional change is in place, so feature acceptance will fail.
